chapter_theme: Pattirakiriyar's lament continues its one question, எக்காலம் (when?), across the inner work: rooting out crooked thought, discerning the tattvas and the three desires, the Shakti in the centre who must reveal herself, the mind cut with the sword of the five letters and watched while it burns, dying before the body dies, and then the breath-yoga in cipher: riding the vaasi instead of walking the earth, rousing the kundalini and opening the sushumna, drinking the milk of the moon-hall, and standing at last with no impurity, no maya, no honour and no clan.
structure_note: Every unit is a couplet closing on எக்காலம், so the reading is what each adds. The stanzas fall in loose runs: 76 to 80 on thought, body and desire; 81 to 83 on birth and the Shakti's grace; 84 to 88 on the mind; 89 to 91 on dying before death; 92 to 98 on the inner path against the outer (ladder, closed eyes, walking, breath, kundalini, sushumna, moon-milk, horse); 99 and 100 on being beyond arts, impurity and clan. Unit 87 is from a different printed source and breaks the running numbering of the நூல் units.

76.reading: When will I have cut out by the root, bond and all, every crooked thought, and remain here knowing the thought that is within?
76.nuance: கள்ளக் கருத்து and உள்ளக் கருத்து are set against each other by rhyme: the deceitful thought is uprooted so that the inner intention (one's own, or the Lord's within) can be known. The same pair, கள்ள மனம் and உள்ளம், returns at 141.

77.reading: When will I discern, part by part, all that I suffered with this body of states that runs riot?
77.nuance: அவத்தை is the technical avastha (the states of waking, dream and the rest through which the soul passes) and also plain Tamil for trouble; அவத்தைச் சடலம் is then either the body that carries the soul through its states or the troublesome body. அட்டகாசம் (uproar, riot) is the body's or the states' unruliness. Both readings leave the same request: to take the body's history apart with understanding.

78.reading: When will I set apart, with the instruments of knowing, all the suffering that the states bring, and grow strong?
78.nuance: அறிவுக் கருவி, the instruments of knowing, is traditionally the inner organs (mind, intellect, will, ego) and the senses, which are tattvas; the verse asks to use them against the states (அவத்தை) they themselves produce. பெலப்படுவது (பலப்படுவது) is simply to become strong; the pair with 77 suggests analysis as the strengthening.

79.reading: When will I know, separating them, the many kinds of difference: the elements, the senses, the inner instruments, and what came as bindu and nada?
79.nuance: The list runs up the tattva ladder from the gross elements (பூதம்) through the senses (பொறி) and inner organs (கரணம்) to bindu and nada, the subtle sources of form and sound. The request is tattva-discrimination, the knowing that these are not the self; the verse does not name what is left when they are set apart.

80.reading: When will I know the three desires that arise, having parted from them, and when will I cut through, at its base, the root of the desire that has sunk in?
80.nuance: ஆசை மூன்று, the three desires, is a fixed triad in the tradition, மண் பொன் பெண் (land, gold, woman); the verse does not list them. தோன்றாசை (the desire that appears) and ஊன்றாசை (the desire that has taken root) distinguish the arising from the entrenched, and only the second is to be cut at the root.

81.reading: When will I know, before cherishing this lowly birth, that if the turning circle goes, my birth will then prosper?
81.nuance: புரிவட்டம், the twisted or turning circle, is unexplained: it may be the round of births, the womb, or, in the breath-cipher, the circling of the breath. புன்சனனம் போற்று முன்னே is also open: 'before I cherish this mean birth' or 'before this mean birth that I cherish'. ஈடேறும் (will be saved, will prosper) is the one firm point: the present birth is to be made to count.

82.reading: When will the good Tirodhayi, standing in the very centre, show the way to come near grace and act in mercy?
82.nuance: திரோதாயி is the concealing power (tirodhana shakti), the Lord's act of hiding; Saiva tradition holds that the same power, once the soul ripens, turns to grace, which is why the poet can call her நல் (good) and ask her for the way to grace. நட்ட நடு, the exact centre, is read by the yoga tradition as the central channel or the point between the brows; plainly it is simply where she stands within.

83.reading: I have stayed saying 'I myself am I'; when will the beautiful one who stands in the centre say 'I myself will reveal it and give it'?
83.nuance: The two நானே balance each other: the poet's self-assertion and the Shakti's promise. கட்டழகி, the perfect beauty standing in the middle, continues the feminine power of 82 at the centre of the body; the revelation is hers to make, not his to seize.

84.reading: When will I cut and burn the dense forest of the mind, striking again and again with the sword that is the five letters?
84.nuance: The mantra is a weapon against the mind rather than an offering to the Lord, and the cutting must be repeated (தொடர்ந்து தொடர்ந்து). The sword of letters returns at 117, where the letters va and ma become the blade.

85.reading: When will I watch this waste mind, that wanders by the paths of the five senses, fall burnt, and wake?
85.nuance: பாழ்மனம், the waste or ruined mind, is burnt and watched falling; the poet is the onlooker, and விழிப்பது, waking, is his own event after the mind's death. The stanza continues the burning of 84.

86.reading: When will I have discerned grace, so that kin die, all who have gathered round die of themselves, and anger dies and goes?
86.nuance: The string of மாண்டு (dying) makes the grammar loose: 'kin, the gathered, oneself and anger' may all be subjects that die, or the kin may literally die while the rest die figuratively. Read with 87, the deaths are inner, the ending of ties and passions through grace rather than the death of relatives.

87.reading: When will anger die, speech and action die, the 'I' die, the mind die, and the state of release come and be reached?
87.nuance: This unit comes from a different printed source and completes the chain of மாண்டு begun in 86: anger, speech, deed, I, mind, each dying in turn, with release as what arrives of itself when they are gone. The 'I' (நான்) dies before the mind.

88.reading: When will the mind that will not settle settle, and when will I see the house of bliss and stay there gazing without blinking?
88.nuance: இமையாமல் நோக்கி, the unblinking gaze, is a mark of the yogic trance in the tradition; the house (வீடு) is release. The settling of the mind comes first and the seeing follows.

89.reading: When will I have died already, before the soul in its cage falls dead, slowly, as with a yawn?
89.nuance: கூண்டு, the cage, is the body; the yawn (கொட்டாவி) is the slow last breath. To die before dying is the Siddhar's state of the living dead, the self already gone while the body stands, taken up again at 90, 126 and 139.

90.reading: When will the day come for me to die, before this body full of flesh loses its life and goes?
90.nuance: A plain restatement of 89 with the body as ஊன் நிறைந்த காயம், the flesh-filled frame. நான் இறந்து போக is the death of the 'I', not of the body, which has its own later death.

91.reading: When will I have burnt myself, before the people who themselves will perish come speaking their boasts and burn me?
91.nuance: சுடு carries both senses at once: the mourners, or the proud, will cremate the body; the poet wants to have burnt himself first, in austerity or in the fire of knowledge, as the mind was burnt at 84 and 85. கெர்விதம் (garvita, pride, boasting) could also be the empty consolations spoken at a death.

92.reading: When will I look by climbing the ladder of the thread, instead of climbing the ladder of skin and walking far until I am worn out?
92.nuance: தோல் ஏணி, the leather ladder, is the body, worn out by walking to shrines; நூல் ஏணி is either the ladder of books (the scripture that shows the way) or the ladder of thread, which the yoga tradition reads as the fine central channel one climbs within. The contrast of outer journey and inner ascent holds on either reading, and the next stanzas (93, 94) repeat it.

93.reading: When will I close my eyes with the Mother and stand embracing her, instead of standing with eyes closed and mouth busy, lost in a daze?
93.nuance: The rhyme வாயோடு / தாயோடு carries the point: the show of meditation (eyes shut, mouth reciting, mind in a stupor) against the real closing of the eyes in union with the Mother, the Shakti. மயக்கம் can be plain drowsiness or delusion.

94.reading: When will I ride the vaasi and come, instead of walking the whole earth until my feet give out?
94.nuance: வாசி is the breath, and in the Siddhars' usage the breath-practice itself; the tradition also hears வாசி as horse (reversing the syllables of சிவா), so riding it is both the breath-yoga and the mount that replaces the pilgrim's feet. The earth walked in vain is the round of shrines.

95.reading: When will I meditate on the kundalini where sound spreads, rouse it by awareness, open the latch of the sushumna and kindle it?
95.nuance: ஒலிபடரும் குண்டலி ties the coiled power to sound, as the tradition does: its rising is heard as nada. தாள் திறந்து, opening the bolt, treats the sushumna as a shut door at the base. The rousing is by உணர்வு, awareness, not by force.

96.reading: When will I stand without obstruction in the sushumna that moves between ida and pingala, and stay there unshaken?
96.nuance: The three channels are named plainly, which makes this the key to the ciphered 144. சலித்தருப்பது is corrupt or unusual: சலித்து can mean to be wearied or to be shaken, so the sense is either 'to remain without being shaken' or, less likely, 'to stay there and tire'; தடை அறவே (without obstruction) favours the first.

97.reading: When will I leave the root fire, kindle it in the hall of the moon, bring down the milk, drink it and end hunger?
97.nuance: A cipher verse: மூலநெருப்பு is the fire at the base (kundalini), நிலா மண்டபம் the moon-hall at the crown, and பால் the nectar the tradition says drips from the moon when the fire reaches it; the hunger ended is bodily (the yogi who no longer needs food) and the soul's. Plainly it is a kitchen scene, fire moved and milk warmed, and the cipher is why it is not one.

98.reading: When will I be in the one space, having let the unbridled horse run into the inner space?
98.nuance: புரவி, the horse, is the breath in the Siddhars' cipher (compare 143) and in common use the restless mind; ஆக வெளி may be the space of the body (ஆக்கை) or the sky (ஆகாய வெளி). On either reading the restless thing is not tied but released into a space, and the poet rests in the ஏக வெளி, the single space beyond.

99.reading: When will I live and move in the reality that the many prattling arts cannot reach, and gain tapas?
99.nuance: பஞ்சரித்துப் பேசும் பல்கலை, the many sciences that chatter, are not condemned as false but as unable to reach (எட்டா) the object; 136 returns to this after the arts have been examined. தவம் here is the attainment, not the means.

100.reading: When will I be, with no impurity and no water, no maya, no honour, no good and no clan?
100.nuance: மலமும் சலமும் is bodily (excrement and urine) and doctrinal (mala, the bond) at once; the list then strips maya, honour (மானம், which is also pride), good fortune (நலம்) and lineage (குலம்). The verse does not say what remains; நான் இருப்பது, 'I being', is the whole of it.

links.note: The Kural says the field of the five senses must be crushed and all that was wanted let go at once; Pattirakiriyar watches the mind that roams by the five senses' paths fall burnt. Both make the senses' mind the thing to be killed, not trained.

The Kural says one who cuts off the pride of 'I' and 'mine' enters a world above the gods; here the 'I' (நான்) dies in the chain that ends in the state of release. Both place the death of the self before the gain.

Kudhambai asks what use hand-cymbals are to the true knower who wanders like the dead; Pattirakiriyar asks when he will have died before the soul leaves the cage. The same figure of the living dead, as a question in one and a state in the other.

Tirumular's inner fire, for those who reach the young crescent, becomes a thread-ladder (நூலேணி) for the ready mind; Pattirakiriyar wants to climb the நூல் ஏணி instead of the ladder of skin. If நூல் is thread in both, the image is the same inner ascent; if the pulambal means books, it is a different ladder.

Tirumular says riding the horse swifter than a bird gives joy without toddy and drives off sloth; Pattirakiriyar wants to ride the vaasi instead of wearing out his feet on the earth. Both make the breath a mount, and both set it against a slower bodily motion.

Tirumular has the kalas run through ida, pingala and the unnamed middle channel, and the good rouse the base and join it to the head; Pattirakiriyar rouses the kundalini by awareness and opens the sushumna's latch. The same operation, with the pulambal adding that the opening is a shut door.

Tirumular says moon and sun rise and fall through ida and pingala and life wells up in the middle between them; Pattirakiriyar asks to stand unobstructed in the sushumna that moves between the two. Both locate the gain in the middle, not in either side channel.

Tirumular says that when the fire at the root of the central channel drives the sun and lets the moon drink, the higher siddhis come; Pattirakiriyar leaves the root fire, kindles it in the moon-hall and drinks the milk. The same cipher of fire, moon and drink, with the pulambal's gain being the end of hunger rather than powers.

Tirumular says that for those who set Nandi in love by knowledge there is no impurity, no stain, no pride, no clan, no qualities and no good to seek; Pattirakiriyar asks when he will be without impurity, maya, honour, good and clan. Nearly the same list, as a description in one and a longing in the other.

source_issues: 87 (siddhar:meynjanap-pulambal:0155-88) is from a different printed source (pmuni0155, numbered 88 there) and is not among the நூல் units; it fits between 86 and 88 as the continuation of 86's chain of மாண்டு, and may be a stanza the main source omits.
95 line 1 has a broken word, கு ண்டலியை, for குண்டலியை.
96 line 2 சலித்தருப்பது is corrupt or irregular; சலித்திருப்பது or சலியாதிருப்பது is likely.
